case_name: Seema Devi vs Shree Ranjit Kumar Bhagat
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1998 and had a child. Disputes arose, leading the husband to file for divorce. The wife was proceeded ex parte and an ex parte decree of divorce was passed. The wife then filed an application to set aside the ex parte judgment.

legal_principles.principle: The service of summons may be made by delivering or transmitting a copy thereof by registered post acknowledgment due, addressed to the defendant or his agent empowered to accept the service.
legal_principles.held: The services of summons may be made by delivering or transmitting a copy thereof by registered post acknowledgment due, addressed to the defendant or his agent empowered to accept the service or by speed post or by such courier services as are approved by the Court referred to in sub-rule (1) or by any other means of transmission of documents.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order V

legal_principles.principle: The service of summons shall be made at the expenses of the plaintiff.
legal_principles.held: Provided that the service of summons under this sub-rule shall be made at the expenses of the plaintiff.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order V

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed, and the order dismissing the application to set aside the ex parte judgment is set aside.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
